questions.title: How long have you used Claude Code?
questions.hint: This changes a few helpers for new users.

options.label: I am new to Claude Code.
options.hint: The /init command asks you before it writes files.

options.label: I have used it for a few weeks.
options.hint: Shows full thinking summaries. The /init command asks before it writes files.

options.label: I use it every day.
options.hint: Shows full thinking summaries and hides the gray prompt suggestions.

questions.title: What extra data may Claude Code send?
questions.hint: Prompts and code always go to the model. This covers extra data only.

options.label: Keep the default: send usage data and error reports.
options.hint: All features keep working. Nothing changes.

options.label: Do not send usage data or error reports.
options.hint: Some features stop working, for example /import and skill sync.

options.label: Send as little as possible, and block claude.ai connectors.
options.hint: No usage data or error reports. Connectors from your claude.ai account do not load.

questions.title: How much does cost matter to you?
questions.hint: This sets the model for helper agents and a limit on effort.

options.label: Spend as little as possible, even if answers get weaker.
options.hint: Helper agents use Haiku unless they ask for another model. Effort is capped at medium.

options.label: Keep costs reasonable without losing much quality.
options.hint: Helper agents use Sonnet unless they ask for another model. Effort is capped at high.

options.label: Quality comes first. Cost is not a concern.
options.hint: Removes limits on effort and on helper models. The prompt cache holds for one hour.

questions.title: What do you do most with Claude Code?

options.label: Large features. I like to plan before Claude writes code.
options.hint: Plans are saved in the project. You can clear context when you accept a plan.

options.label: Many small fixes and quick changes.
options.hint: Claude gives shorter answers.

options.label: Learning a new codebase, language or tool.
options.hint: Claude explains its choices while it works.

questions.title: How much should Claude do without asking you first?
questions.hint: None of these answers lets Claude skip permission checks.

options.label: Ask me before edits and commands, with extra safety checks.
options.hint: Commands run in a sandbox. Reads outside the project and bypass mode are blocked.

options.label: Ask me as usual, and run shell commands in a sandbox.
options.hint: The sandbox limits what commands can touch on your computer.

options.label: Edit files without asking. Keep shell commands in a sandbox.
options.hint: File edits and simple file commands do not ask. Other commands still ask.

questions.title: How many Claude Code sessions do you run at the same time?

options.label: Usually one.
options.hint: Nothing changes.

options.label: Two or three.
options.hint: Uses the fullscreen view without flicker. Shows a recap when you come back.

options.label: Four or more.
options.hint: Sessions start in focus view, with less on screen, and show a recap.

questions.title: How should Claude Code tell you that it is done or needs you?

options.label: Pick the best way for my terminal.
options.hint: Desktop notices in iTerm2, Ghostty and Kitty. Some other terminals get nothing.

options.label: Ring the terminal bell.
options.hint: Works in almost every terminal.

options.label: Do not notify me.
options.hint: You check your sessions yourself.
